title: The worst Jazz Alley show with Eddie Condon
summary: Hodes says the worst show was with Condon, Tony Parenti and others. A two-hour intermission and tired players made it bad.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Now, Smokey played his butt off, played beautifully. And Tony Parenti, in spite of the fact that he was tired, played. But J.C. hadn't been playing, leaning up against the piano, he was tired. And that trip, they came from work without sleep. And then the engineer or somebody at the station, made a mistake. After the rehearsal, they said, fellows, there will be a two-hour intermission.
So the drinkers went out and drank. And there's a

funny story about Eddie Condon I have to tell because he came back with his brother, and we were about ready to go on, and Eddie called me over and said to me, Art, can you talk to the director and see if I can't get my brother to sit on stage with us, because he don't hear so good.
That's right, you had a prop audience.

A prop audience and a small stage. And this was the stage where Pee Wee Russell discovered that the prop bartender looked like a real bartender and started beckoning to him to come over and bring a drink while we were taping, and some very funny things, George Brunis trying to do a Ted Lewis in his hat, Ted Lewis always tumbles his top hat off and catches it and takes a little bow. And George couldn't catch it. On and on and on. We had some funny scenes and some worthwhile things were recorded.

But I guess the show where Eddie was speechless, and I really wanted him to talk. That's really why I got him, because I wanted to get Eddie talking about his life or jazz, any observation. And had he not been in a cast, we could have got some of that. But as it was, the camera man should have got an Oscar for identifying him but missing him, just showing enough of him that it was Eddie Condon, but not showing him the way he looked because he was just out of it. He was just barely sitting there.
And that was the show New York City heard, and they got crazy about it. That was the one. That's the -- in my estimation the worst show. They heard it, called me up.
